source_artifacts.claim: Authored level has a full safe floor, cargo_shelf with a pushable signal_sac, raised bait/finish platforms, no hazards, and nearest-target boomerang with 1.2-second windup/cooldown.
Players can push non-heavy crates and gravity lets them settle on the floor or platforms; the sac can become a step after it falls.
A hero standing on the partner is supported/carries vertically, enabling a partner-as-step boost between elevations.
The authored jump speed/gravity limit a solo rise to about 92 game units; the floor-to-shelf rise is 110, so a partner or raised crate step is needed to reach that shelf from the floor.
Cana’s nearest-target attack locks the closest hero at windup and throws along the locked line.
A boomerang hit gives a hero temporary DIZZY; movement is impaired temporarily, not lethal by itself.

common_mistakes.mistake: Pac jumps beside Isp without landing on the partner before aiming for cargo_shelf.
common_mistakes.consequence: A solo jump cannot cover the 110-unit floor-to-shelf rise; Pac falls back to the broad floor.
common_mistakes.recovery: Reposition beside Isp and use the partner as a step; no progress is permanently lost. Source physics and jump constants support the geometry; native trace demonstrates the stack route, not a failed attempt.

confidence_reason: Source geometry/physics and a current native both-exit route establish a plausible feasible plan, and snapshots include the targeted DIZZY effect. No human first-play route or recovery distribution exists.

confirmed: The partner-lift cue and Cana’s closer-hero attention rule are both central.
The first pass correctly left the sac’s role and attack recovery unresolved from idle captures.
missed_mechanics: The floor-to-shelf rise exceeds a solo jump; Pac steps on Isp to reach the shelf, then pushes the signal sac down so Isp can use it as an intermediate step.
The sac is not required to cross the final glucose_fold or reach the exits; the native completion leaves it on the floor.
Cana locks onto the nearer hero at windup and throws along that line; a hit causes temporary DIZZY, not death.
incorrect_inferences: Pass one proposed staying lower or moving closer to draw attention; the actual system automatically selects the nearest hero at windup, so proximity changes who is targeted rather than being a manually activated control.
Pass one did not know whether the lower floor was dangerous; the source confirms the continuous floor is safe and has no lethal hazards.
changed_judgments: Reasoning remains 2→3 because the actual route links partner boost, crate repositioning, a second partner-assisted climb and a telegraphed targeting response, beyond the visible “lift/slip” phrases.
Cooperation remains 3 but now has concrete reciprocal support: Pac uses Isp as the first step and Isp uses the lowered sac from Pac as the next step; both then cross to separate exits.
Execution remains 2→3 because the route uses multiple elevation transitions and both heroes cross under a DIZZY attack effect; one replay shows feasibility, not typical accuracy.
Timing changes from unknown to 2 because Cana’s aim line/windup provides a repeatable cue to dodge the locked trajectory; the attack repeats and DIZZY is temporary.
Hazards changes from unknown to 0 because no lethal hazard is authored and the lower floor catches missed jumps; DIZZY is movement interference rather than a hazard.
Novelty remains 2 because partner rides from levels_24/_30 and cargo handling from level_25 are familiar; the nearest-target telegraph adds a new combination.

Recovery cost changes from unknown to 1 because failed jumps or short DIZZY effects can be recovered on the continuous floor, with partner/sac climbs repeatable; no full reset is necessary in the source-defined route.
Solution clarity rises 2→3 because the cue names only broad outcomes; it omits the exact two-stage lift using Isp then the lowered sac and the timing response to Cana’s target line.
unresolved: No human evidence establishes how many players will discover or execute the partner/sac step sequence.
The native route demonstrates both exits but does not prove the sac’s placement or the partner boost are the only possible route for an expert.
No direct two-human reliability or control-friction evidence exists; friction stays null.
The scripted attack effects show feasibility but not human difficulty or frustration.

single_operator_note: A single operator would need to stack Pac onto Isp, move Pac across the shelf to relocate the sac, switch to Isp to use the sac and advance, then manage which hero is nearer Cana while both proceed. This is separate from the two-human score; no one-operator trial exists.
